title: Carol Carr
dek_or_short_description: Writer and friend. Frequent correspondence with PKD about writing, personal matters, and publishing.
body_markdown:
Carol Carr was a science fiction writer and friend whose correspondence with PKD reveals something about his values as a reader of other writers' work. PKD, notoriously self-centered in many relationships, took the time to compliment Carr's fiction. "You write neat stories," he told her — a small phrase that carries weight when it comes from a writer as exacting as Dick.

The letters to Carr were personal as well as literary. They exchanged ideas about writing craft and life circumstances, suggesting a friendship grounded in shared creative concerns. In the ecosystem of PKD's relationships, Carr represented the peer writer — not a major figure like Disch or Zelazny, but someone whose work he respected and with whom he could discuss the business and art of fiction.

Like many of the women in PKD's correspondence, Carr's full story remains partially obscured. The surviving letters show professional respect and genuine warmth, but the details of her own career and her relationship with PKD beyond the page remain incomplete in the archive.
summary: Carol Carr (1972–1973+), writer and friend. PKD praised her fiction; frequent correspondence about writing and life.
